# Select

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 1 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For one choice out of a list too long to show at once. For a few short ones, a RadioGroup; for
thousands, or a list to type into, a Combobox. It is one element that takes its options as data.

```tsx
import { Select } from 'topclassui/select'
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor="country">Country</label>
<Select id="country" name="country" items={[{ value: 'jo', label: 'Jordan' }, { value: 'eg', label: 'Egypt' }]} defaultValue="jo" />
```

**A name is required.** `id` for a `<label htmlFor>` (the root hands it to the trigger), or
`aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`; the type refuses a Select with none.

**`items` is plain data**, `{ value, label, disabled? }`, so a server page renders a Select with
no function crossing to the browser. `value` is what the form receives, unique in its list; `label`
is what the row and the trigger show. The trigger prints the label of the value in the server HTML.
An option whose `value` is `''` reads as nothing chosen (Base UI's): the trigger shows the placeholder.

**A Field's props spread onto it**, as they do onto an Input:

```tsx
export function CountryField(control: { id: string, name: string, required: boolean, 'aria-describedby': string, 'aria-invalid': boolean }) {
  return <Select {...control} items={[{ value: 'jo', label: 'Jordan' }]} />
}
```

**The state.** `value` and `defaultValue` are a string, or `null` for nothing chosen; `onValueChange`
gets the same and Base UI's details. Your handler runs first, so `details.cancel()` keeps the value.
Nothing chosen shows `placeholder`, or `select.placeholder` from the provider's labels.

**The form.** With a `name`, a hidden input sends `name=<value>`, and `name=` with nothing chosen.
Before the page hydrates it sends the default. **A form reset**, a reset button or a React 19 form
action that settles brings it back to the `defaultValue` of the latest render, on screen and in
the form; a controlled Select keeps its owner's value. A reset calls no `onValueChange`.
**`required`** with nothing chosen blocks a submit. Before the page hydrates the browser then
sends the focus to the hidden input, a box of 1 px; after it, to the trigger.

**The keyboard.** Tab stops on the trigger. ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Space or Enter open the list
with the focus on the chosen option, scrolled into view. The arrows move and stop at both ends;
Home and End jump. A disabled option takes the focus but Enter does nothing on it. Enter chooses
and closes; Escape closes. The focus comes back to the trigger. A letter typed on the closed
trigger chooses the next option that starts with it. The arrows of a list are vertical: they mean
the same in Arabic.

**The list** is seven rows tall (`--tc-list-rows`), or `visibleRows` (1 to 20), and scrolls inside
itself; the page behind does not move. A row is 40 px, 44 px under a finger. It is at least as wide
as the trigger when there is room, and grows with its longest label up to the room on screen; a longer label ends in
an ellipsis, in the row and in the trigger. **It is not windowed**: Base UI mounts every option
once the trigger takes the focus. For thousands of options use a Combobox.

**The width** belongs to a box around the trigger: the width of an Input of the same `size`, and
less when the parent is narrower. `fullWidth` fills the parent. A width class in `className` lands
on the trigger inside the box: use `fullWidth` and size the parent. In a parent that sizes to its
content (a `w-fit` box, a table cell) there is nothing to fill: give the parent a width.

**`placement`** takes the twelve shared values, `bottom-start` by default; `start` and `end` are
the reading sides. The list opens 6 px off the trigger, flips at an edge and stays 8 px inside the
screen. It never covers the trigger: a side placement whose list does not fit beside the trigger, as
beside one on a phone, opens below it, or above, as wide as the trigger.

**`modal`** is Base UI's:
- `true`, the default: while the list is open the page does not scroll and a press outside only closes it.
- `false`: the page scrolls and takes presses while the list is open.

**Escape** closes the list first; a second one closes the Dialog around it.

**`invalid`** sets `aria-invalid` on the trigger: its line turns red and thickens. **`disabled`**
is the real attribute, so the form sends nothing. **`readOnly`** keeps the value in the form and
takes the soft fill, and in forced colours, which drop a fill, a dashed line; the list opens but
no option can be chosen.

**Arabic.** The caret and the tick sit at the left, and `bottom-start` lines the list up with the
right edge of the trigger. The list takes its direction and language from the nearest
`TopClassProvider`, also in an island; with none, those of the page.

**On the element.** `className`, `style`, `ref`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and the rest
go to the trigger, a `<button role="combobox">`. The box around it takes nothing from you.

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `Select.Root`, `Trigger`, `Value`, `Icon`, `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Popup`, `List`, `Item`, `ItemText`, `ItemIndicator` | one `Select` |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` with `details.cancel()` | the same names, a string or `null`; the value is held for the form reset |
| `items`, any shape | `{ value, label, disabled? }` only, mapped to one `Item` each |
| `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `inputRef`, `autoComplete`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal`, `highlightItemOnHover` | passed through |
| `alignItemWithTrigger`, true by default | always `false`, so `placement` and the shared offsets apply |
| `multiple`, `itemToStringLabel`, `itemToStringValue`, `isItemEqualToValue` | not props |

### Not built

The parts as exports (`SelectRoot`, `SelectItem`), `multiple` (MultiSelect is its own row), groups
and separators, an icon or a second line in an option, remote options and loading states,
windowing, the scroll arrows, `variant`, a Drawer on a phone, a clear button or an empty option
(a chosen value cannot be unset by the user), `selectedItem`, a warning for two options with one
`value`, a skeleton (use `InputSkeleton`).

## Import

```tsx
import { Select } from 'topclassui/select'
```

## Props

Required: `items`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` or `id`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | **yes** | `readonly ListOption[]` | - | Plain data, so a Server Component can render a Select: one option per row, in order. |
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` or `id` | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible label names the control. |
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `id` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the control. |
| `id` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The id a `<label htmlFor>` points at. |
| `className` | no | `string` | - | On the trigger, merged last, so a consumer class wins a conflict with its own. |
| `container` | no | `Base.Portal.Props['container']` | - | Where the list mounts; `<body>` by default. |
| `fullWidth` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Select: the box fills the width of its parent instead of taking the width of an Input. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Select: marks the choice as wrong: sets aria-invalid on the trigger, whose line turns to danger and thickens. |
| `placeholder` | no | `string` | - | The text of an empty trigger. Left out, the provider's `select.placeholder`. |
| `placement` | no | `top` \| `top-start` \| `top-end` \| `bottom` \| `bottom-start` \| `bottom-end` \| `start` \| `start-top` \| `start-bottom` \| `end` \| `end-top` \| `end-bottom` | `"bottom-start"` | Select: the side and alignment the list opens at; start and end mirror in Arabic. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | - | The trigger, a `<button role="combobox">`. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | Select: the height, the inline padding and the type step of the trigger, and its width with them; custom emits no size classes. |
| `visibleRows` | no | `number`, min 1, max 20 | `7` | Select: rows the list shows before it scrolls, clamped; left out, the --tc-list-rows knob applies. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
